query: What are the common advantage attributes of airlines whose overall rating is high?

per_column.name: crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Quality of crew/staff service is a genuine constitutive aspect of an airline's competitive advantage in service delivery.

per_column.name: crew_above_and_beyond
per_column.rationale: Exceptional discretionary crew effort is an aspect of service advantage, though it overlaps heavily with crew_service_quality (the 'exceptional' level captures the same phenomenon).

per_column.name: personalized_service
per_column.rationale: Personalization is a distinct dimension of service advantage, though partly overlapping with crew quality/above-and-beyond.

per_column.name: service_consistency
per_column.rationale: Reliability/consistency of service delivery is a legitimate aspect of the advantage, and reasonably distinct from raw quality.

per_column.name: food_quality
per_column.rationale: Catering quality is a core product facet of an airline's offering and advantage.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_perception
per_column.rationale: Seat/cabin comfort is a core constitutive facet of the flying-experience advantage.

per_column.name: ife_quality
per_column.rationale: Inflight entertainment is a distinct product facet of the onboard advantage.

per_column.name: amenity_provision
per_column.rationale: Provision of amenities is a distinct tangible facet of the onboard product advantage.

judge.rationale: All added columns are genuine part-of facets of 'airline competitive advantage' as an onboard service/product concept; none are external predictors, causes, or restatements of the whole. Mutual exclusivity is moderate: the four crew/service columns (crew_service_quality, crew_above_and_beyond, personalized_service, service_consistency) overlap substantially, with 'above_and_beyond' and 'personalized' largely subsumed by the quality dimension, over-weighting the human-service aspect. Exhaustiveness is fairly good for the onboard-experience dimensions (crew, food, seat, IFE, amenities) but misses other constitutive facets of competitive advantage such as value-for-money/price, on-time performance/reliability, route network/schedule, and booking/ground experience, so it captures the product-experience portion but not the full concept.
